title: Weighted on-call simulation harness and safe auto-remediation hooks
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Add a weighted on-call simulation harness and pluggable, safety-first auto-remediation hooks for incident-bot. This PR provides: a simulator that replays historical alert streams with configurable weighting and stochastic responder availability; a policy layer that scores simulated on-call load against team rotas and SLOs; and an opt-in auto-remediation hook framework with guardrails (dry-run mode, rate limits, circuit breaker, and audit logging).

Motivation:
On-call fatigue and poorly calibrated automatic remediation have caused slow MTTR and a handful of bad rollbacks in Q2/Q3. We need an offline way for teams to: 1) model the effect of changing schedules or escalation policies, 2) surface dangerous remediation rules before they run in production, and 3) provide a safe runtime path for low-risk automated mitigations during incidents.

Design highlights:
- Simulator: accepts historical alert slices, supports weighting strategies (by service, severity, origin region), and simulates responder availability windows; outputs metrics aligned with our SLO definitions.
- Policy layer: pluggable scoring functions for responder load, fatigue, and correlated failures; can run bulk experiments to find escalation thresholds that minimize MTTR without increasing false auto-remediations.
- Auto-remediation hooks: new hook interface (OncallAutoRemediate) with enforced contracts: requires a pre-approve dry-run result, a rate limiter token bucket per-hook, a team-level circuit breaker that trips on anomalous rollback counts, signed audit events to the audit-log-exporter sink, and an opt-in label in team config.
- Safety-first defaults: all hooks default to dry-run; enabling requires an explicit team-level flag and a two-person approval for production enablement.

What changed (high-level files):
- internal/oncall/sim/driver.go (new): core simulator loop and weighting strategies.
- internal/oncall/weighting.go (new): weighting strategies and config parsing.
- cmd/oncall-sim/main.go (new): CLI to run local/backfill simulations and export summaries.
- internal/hooks/autoremediate.go (new): hook interface, safeties, and wrappers for dry-run and token bucket.
- webhooks/autoremediate-adapter.go (modified): adapter to call hook implementations and persist audit records.
- docs/oncall-sim.md (new): usage and example experiments.
- tests/sim/sim_integration_test.go (new): deterministic simulation golden tests and load scenarios.
- tests/hooks/autoremediate_safety_test.go (new): tests for rate limiting, circuit breaking, and audit emission.

Commits (summary):
- feat(sim): initial simulator skeleton and replay harness
- feat(sim): add weighting strategies and responder model
- feat(hooks): define OncallAutoRemediate interface and dry-run wrapper
- fix(tests): stabilize flaky timing in sim integration test (use fake clock)
- ci: add pipeline job `sim-integration` to run golden sim tests

Testing & CI:
- Added unit and integration tests covering the main safety properties.
- New pipeline job `sim-integration` runs golden scenario replay and compares output metrics.
- Initial CI run failed on timing-sensitive sim test (flake); I switched the sim internals to use a fake clock and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, sim-integration, e2e-mocks).

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main in squash mode.
- Feature is behind config:teams.<team>.enable_autoremediate (default: false).
- Enable dry-run experiments for a handful of SRE teams on staging for 2 weeks, run simulations against last 30 days of alerts.
- After validation, enable limited production opt-ins with telemetry and a manual approval gate.

Backward compatibility and migrations:
- No schema migrations required.
- New audit events are additive and consumed by audit-log-exporter; consumers must be tolerant of new event types.

Related:
- ENG-1292 (on-call tooling roadmap), SUP-4421 (customer report about unsafe automated rollbacks), ENG-1338 (observability for remediation actions).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for weighting strategies
- [x] Integration/golden tests for simulator
- [x] Safety tests for hooks (rate limiting, circuit breaker)
- [x] Docs and runbook examples
- [x] CI job added

Notes:
- The simulator CLI supports a `--dry-run` that emits artifacts to stdout or S3; example in docs.
- We intentionally overload the simulator to be deterministic when given a seed for reproducible experiments.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez (review): Please add a kill-switch env var and document how on-call teams can revoke hook entitlements. Also add a short-form audit event for the UI team.
Maya Chen (author): Added TEAM_AUTOREMEDIATE_KILL_SWITCH and documented revocation flow; added lightweight audit event 'autoremediate:decision' that the UI team can consume.
Priya Nair (review): Tests look good. Suggest lowering default token-bucket rate (rate=1/min) to reduce blast radius for initial experiments.
Maya Chen (author): Lowered default rate to 1/min and added per-hook override. Also added circuit-breaker thresholds and unit tests for trip conditions.
Samir Patel (review): CI flaked on sim integration due to real-time sleeps — thanks for moving to fake clock. Approving after CI green.
